claims: There have been seven documented ties in Oscar history.
The most recent tie occurred at the 98th Academy Awards in 2026.
Oscar ties span acting, documentary, sound, and short film categories.
At the 98th Academy Awards in 2026, Best Live Action Short Film tied between The Singers and Two People Exchanging Saliva.
At the 85th Academy Awards in 2013, Best Sound Editing tied between Skyfall (Per Hallberg and Karen Baker Landers) and Zero Dark Thirty (Paul N.J. Ottosson).
At the 67th Academy Awards in 1995, Best Live Action Short Film tied between Franz Kafka’s It’s a Wonderful Life and Trevor.
At the 59th Academy Awards in 1987, Best Documentary Feature tied between Artie Shaw: Time Is All You’ve Got and Down and Out in America.
At the 41st Academy Awards in 1969, Best Actress tied between Katharine Hepburn (The Lion in Winter) and Barbra Streisand (Funny Girl).
At the 22nd Academy Awards in 1950, Best Documentary (Short Subject) tied between A Chance to Live and So Much for So Little.
At the 5th Academy Awards in 1932, Best Actor tied between Fredric March (Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde) and Wallace Beery (The Champ).
Fredric March had one more vote than Wallace Beery in the 5th Academy Awards Best Actor category.
Rules at the time of the 5th Academy Awards mandated a tie if nominees were within three votes of each other.
The 2013 Sound Editing tie prompted a surprise announcement by presenter Mark Wahlberg.
Mark Wahlberg assured the audience it was "No B.S.!".
The 2026 tie was the second time in history the Best Live Action Short category resulted in a tie.
